Definition: to be strong; by implication, to prevail, act insolently
BiblicalUsage: Gabar means to be strong, to prevail, and it decides battles and covenants alike. Judah prevailed above his brethren in 1 Chronicles 5:2, and Hannah sang that by strength shall no man prevail in 1 Samuel 2:9. The messenger told David the men prevailed against Israel in 2 Samuel 11:23, and Daniel sees a prince who shall confirm the covenant with many in Daniel 9:27.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe prevailing is never a matter of strength alone. Hannah knew it when she sang that no man prevails by strength, and I hold that the victories that last are the ones God wins for His people.
